question: Is there a specific, plausible decision in the screen / verify / stop allocation problem where an LLM could add value beyond the strongest deterministic scheduler with equivalent information?

prior_evidence.gate_test: WS4 gate (O'Neil, exposed development data, 39 lines x 4 rounds, deepseek-flash, 312 valid calls, USD 0.1384): with true scores the LLM re-sorts by displayed score (82% of picks = displayed-score top k; 94% explained by order or score); with permuted scores, LLM minus first-k-presented = +0.08 [-0.87, 0.97] hits per line; residual picks hit at 0.127-0.150 against a menu base rate of 0.155
prior_evidence.registered_status: MODIFY under its registered rule (intervals cannot exclude up to ~1 hit per line) - inconclusive, not evidence of benefit; evaluation was one-step on deterministic histories, not the LLM's own history
prior_evidence.literature: Gupta, Hartford & Liu 2025 (EMNLP; arXiv 2509.21403): permuted outcome labels do not change LLM-agent performance in BO; Wainrib et al. 2026 (arXiv 2603.26177): feedback use only for the strongest model tested (both verified by WS4)

candidate_decisions_examined.decision: which screen hits to verify (and in what order)
candidate_decisions_examined.deterministic_strongest: verify every unverified hit, ordered by historical P(confirm | hit) per cost (allocation arm conf_per_cost) or by screen label
candidate_decisions_examined.information_an_llm_could_add: mechanism-level knowledge of which drug classes give orientation- or plate-specific artefacts
candidate_decisions_examined.why_not_plausible: that knowledge is either in the history (pair and drug confirmation rates, which the deterministic rule already uses) or is literature knowledge of the published Jaaks results, which cannot be separated from memorisation on any public dataset; the decision space is tiny (about 2-4 unverified hits per line per round), so the room for any selector is bounded by the scheduler-only ceiling (+9.6% at the Jaaks budget)

candidate_decisions_examined.decision: when to stop screening / reserve terminal verification capacity
candidate_decisions_examined.deterministic_strongest: a development-selected reserve rule (allocation plan: reserve sized from history screen-call probabilities; fixed split f selected leave-one-tissue-out)
candidate_decisions_examined.why_not_plausible: a one-dimensional threshold decision on numbers already in the state; the gate showed the model reproduces displayed numbers rather than adding information; a tuned threshold is the natural optimum for such a decision
this is exactly the selector role tested by the WS4 gate (no detectable knowledge beyond displayed scores); on Jaaks any apparent knowledge is confounded with memorisation of a 2022 publication

why_a_diagnostic_would_not_be_informativ: no qualified untouched dataset exists (data_qualification.json); on exposed public data an LLM gain cannot be separated from memorisation
power: a 5% gain needs about 146-245 lines (statistics.json); Jaaks has 125, so even a perfectly run own-history LLM arm would most likely return UNRESOLVED
the strongest deterministic scheduler is not yet fixed: the allocation replay has not reported, so the comparator an LLM must beat is undefined
what_would_reopen_it: a qualified, unpublished (or post-training-cutoff) dataset with the full action menu
a decision that requires information outside the numeric state, named in advance, with a deterministic version of the same information as the comparator (information equivalence)
a stronger model with documented feedback use on held-out data

reference_sketch_if_ever_reopened.status: NOT A PLAN TO RUN; for cost reference only
reference_sketch_if_ever_reopened.design: own-history campaigns: the LLM makes the verify/stop decision each round from its own purchased history; comparator = the registered strongest deterministic scheduler on identical state text; arms differ only in the decision-maker
reference_sketch_if_ever_reopened.calls: 125 lines x 2 role assignments x 4 decision rounds = 1,000 first-attempt calls (+ <= 1 retry each)
reference_sketch_if_ever_reopened.cost_estimate_usd: about 0.44 first attempts at the WS4 gate's observed USD 0.00044 per call; <= 0.9 with every call retried; above the USD 1 cap if prompts grow beyond about 2x the gate's
reference_sketch_if_ever_reopened.stop_rule: single run; STOP if the upper 95% bound of (LLM minus deterministic) is below +5% or if >= 90% of decisions equal the deterministic rule's; no prompt iteration after an inconclusive result
